g.text: DNSSEC chain of trust for example.com
✓ DNSSEC is on and validates for example.com
Every link from the root down to example.com is signed and checks out: each parent vouches for its
child's key with a DS record, and each zone signs its records with that key. DNSSEC protects against
forged DNS answers: someone on the network, or a poisoned resolver cache, can't send visitors to a
fake address without the signature check failing. It doesn't encrypt DNS or hide which sites you
visit. Validating resolvers (such as 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9) check this automatically.
Nothing to do. When you change DNS host or keys, update the DS record at the registrar at
the same time, or validation breaks.
